questions.question: k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) is an example of an eager learning method.
questions.reasoning: k-NN is a lazy learning or instance-based method that delays processing until a test instance is given.

questions.question: Instance-based learning (lazy learning) is generally faster during training but slower during classification compared to eager learning.
questions.reasoning: Lazy methods spend less time in training but more time in predicting/classification.

questions.question: In the vanilla k-NN algorithm, the label assigned to a test point is determined by taking the average of the labels of the k nearest neighbors.
questions.reasoning: The vanilla k-NN returns the majority label of the k nearest neighbors for classification.

questions.question: The distance-weighted k-NN approach assigns equal weight to all k nearest neighbors regardless of their distance to the test point.
questions.reasoning: Distance-weighted k-NN weighs neighbors according to their distance, downplaying the labels of neighbors that are farther away.

questions.question: For real-valued prediction (regression), the k-NN approach returns the mean value of the k nearest neighbors.
questions.reasoning: k-NN for real-valued prediction returns the mean values of the k nearest neighbors.
